skill.name: blocklet-converter
skill.description: Converts static web or Next.js projects into ArcBlock Blocklets with DID validation, metadata extraction, asset preparation, and packaging checks.
skill.summary: Convert static web and Next.js projects into ArcBlock Blocklets.
skill.author: ArcBlock

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown code fences, documented examples, runtime Blocklet variables, and the ArcBlock store URL. I confirmed the command risk where the skill instructs agents to install dependencies, build projects, and run Blocklet CLI packaging. No evidence found of credential exfiltration, malicious network calls, or prompt injection.

remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before running install, build, metadata, or bundling commands. Show the exact commands before execution.

remediation.issue: Runtime environment variables in the Next.js entry file
remediation.suggestion: Document BLOCKLET_MODE, BLOCKLET_APP_DIR, and BLOCKLET_PORT. Warn users not to place secrets in these variables.

remediation.issue: Hardcoded ArcBlock store URL in the static template
remediation.suggestion: Document why the store URL is trusted, or make it configurable for private Blocklet deployments.
Publish a checksum or source asset for the default PNG so reviewers can verify future changes quickly.

content.value_statement: Turning a web app into a Blocklet requires correct metadata, assets, build output, and packaging commands. This skill guides Claude, Codex, or Claude Code through a repeatable conversion workflow.
actual_capabilities: Detects static web apps and Next.js apps from package files, HTML entries, or framework configs.
Validates a required Blocklet DID before conversion starts.
Builds supported projects when a build script exists and stops on failures.
Creates or copies README, logo, Next.js entry, and blocklet.yml assets.
Runs Blocklet CLI verification and bundle commands for the selected project type.
Emits project title and description markers for downstream tools.
limitations: Supports only static web apps and Next.js projects, not backend services.
Requires a valid pre-generated Blocklet DID from the user.
Assumes required build tools and the Blocklet CLI are installed.
Running dependency installs and builds can execute target project scripts.

use_cases.title: Package a Static Frontend
use_cases.description: Convert a Vite, React, or plain HTML project into a Blocklet with generated metadata and assets.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Next.js Blocklet
use_cases.description: Add the required Next.js entry file and Blocklet configuration before bundling the app.

use_cases.title: Standardize Release Packaging
use_cases.description: Apply a repeatable conversion checklist before teams publish web apps to ArcBlock infrastructure.

prompt_templates.title: Convert Current Project
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner conversion with a known DID.
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert this project into an ArcBlock Blocklet using DID z8iaExampleDid. Validate the project first and stop if requirements are missing.

prompt_templates.title: Convert a Static Site
prompt_templates.scenario: Static web app with build output.
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert this static web app into a Blocklet. Find the correct output directory, prepare missing assets, and verify the Blocklet metadata.

prompt_templates.title: Convert a Next.js App
prompt_templates.prompt: Detect whether this is a Next.js project, add the required entry file, generate the Blocklet configuration, and run verification.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose Conversion Failures
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this project for Blocklet conversion readiness. Explain blockers, fix only conversion issues, then continue packaging when safe.

output_examples.input: A Vite React project with a valid Blocklet DID.
output_examples.output: The skill confirms a static web app, builds it, creates Blocklet metadata, validates the result, and prepares a release bundle.

output_examples.input: A Next.js project that needs Blocklet packaging.
output_examples.output: The skill creates the Next.js entry file, prepares configuration and assets, validates metadata, and bundles the app with Next.js settings.

output_examples.input: A project with a failing TypeScript build.
output_examples.output: The skill stops conversion, reports the build failure, and avoids creating release files until the project is fixed.

best_practices: Review package scripts before allowing dependency installation or builds.
Generate and verify the Blocklet DID before invoking the skill.
Review generated metadata and included files before publishing the bundle.
anti_patterns: Do not use this skill for backend API services or unsupported server frameworks.
Do not run conversion in projects with untrusted install or build scripts.
Do not publish generated bundles before reviewing Blocklet configuration and assets.

faq.question: Can this skill generate a Blocklet DID?
faq.answer: No. It requires a pre-generated DID from the user before conversion starts.

faq.question: Does it support Next.js projects?
faq.answer: Yes. It detects Next.js projects and adds the entry file needed for Blocklet packaging.

faq.question: Does it support backend services?
faq.answer: No. It exits when it detects backend frameworks such as Express, Koa, Fastify, or Nest.

faq.question: What files can it create or copy?
faq.answer: It can prepare README, logo, Blocklet configuration, and the Next.js entry file when needed.

faq.question: Will it run commands?
faq.answer: Yes. It may install dependencies, build the project, validate metadata, and create a bundle.

faq.question: What should I check before publishing?
faq.answer: Review generated metadata, included files, build output, and any scripts that ran during conversion.
